nodes.label: Stage 32 — Speaking modern MCP as well as legacy (implemented)
nodes.rationale: Written down in Stage 31 as a cheap version bump, and that was wrong. 2026-07-28 is a modern revision with no initialize handshake at all: version in per-request _meta plus a header, no session, a mandatory server/discover, resultType on every result, -32022 for an unsupported version, and notifications on a subscriptions/listen stream. Dual-era is the target, not migration: claude.ai is a legacy client, and a legacy client against a modern-only server simply fails with no fall-forward.

nodes.label: Per-request _meta selects modern, not the header
nodes.rationale: A legacy client sends MCP-Protocol-Version on every request after its handshake, so treating the header's presence as modern intent would have reclassified every connector already talking to this endpoint. A request with no _meta is served exactly as before, header or no header. An unknown version in _meta is an error, not a fallback: the first cut fell through to legacy and served shapes the client never asked for, and the acceptance test for -32022 caught it.

nodes.label: Legacy results returned byte for byte untouched
nodes.rationale: `decorate` adds resultType and the per-response serverInfo only on the modern path, and the legacy initialize result is asserted field for field in the spec, because the cost of getting this wrong is every existing connector. The existing MCP request specs passing unchanged is the real test.

nodes.label: listChanged stays false, deliberately
nodes.rationale: Declaring a capability the server cannot honour is worse than declaring none: a client that trusts listChanged: true will never re-fetch, because it believes it will be told. GET /mcp is 405 and the server pushes nothing; a stream per connected client is a capacity question before it is a protocol one. It is also not worth much, since ttlMs: 0 already tells clients not to cache and the rules ride on every result.

nodes.label: Header/body agreement is enforced, including Mcp-Name
nodes.rationale: The transport mirrors method and params.name into headers so intermediaries can route without parsing the body; skipping validation would leave exactly the hole the headers introduce, a proxy rate-limiting or routing on the header while the server acts on the body. Base64 sentinel values are decoded before comparison.
